findings: Full-model FSDP2 GRPO on SkyRL mirrored verl's hyperparameters (batch 16 / group 8 / lr 1e-5 / kl 0.04 / temp 0.7 / max_tokens 256 / max_prompt 4096 / 1 epoch), but the training reward collapsed to 0.0 (pass@8=0.0) over the final steps instead of improving.

eval_before_train was 0.329 (the checkpoint emits valid triplets), unlike verl's 0.0 (thinking-disabled SFT emitting empty output) — so the two baselines are not directly comparable; verl is a 0->0.715 learning demo, SkyRL is a 0.329->0.0 forgetting failure.

The final HF-weight save OOM'd: cpu_offload=true pins ~180GB (params + fp32 AdamW + master weights), and save_hf_model consolidated the full model on top, pushing RAM to 185.8/186.7GB. Ray killed a worker at 99.5% and infinite-retried, so eval_interval=16 never ran and no final weights were written.
ckpt_interval=0 + hf_save_interval=16 was set to avoid the ~53GB full checkpoint (bf16 weights + fp32 optimizer) on a disk with limited free space; the HF-weights-only save is what OOM'd.
256 train frames / batch 16 nominally yields 16 steps; the log records 15 completed steps (global_step 1-15, 15 rollout rewards) before the final save OOM'd.
estimated_cost_usd and wall_time_s are approximate (g5.12xlarge on-demand ~$5.67/hr, ~3.75h for the RL run) and exclude the extensive pre-run debugging/smoke tests on the same instance.

Re-run 2026-11-13: completed cleanly (state=succeeded, FULL_EXIT=0) after fixing the OOM — ckpt_interval=0 + hf_save_interval=0 (no epoch-end HF save), SKYRL_WAIT_UNTIL_INFERENCE_SERVER_HEALTHY_TIMEOUT_S=1800 (vLLM health timeout), NVIDIA driver 595 (torch resolved to cu13). 16 steps (no prompts filtered at max_prompt_length=4096), final val eval avg_score=0.0, and the training rollout reward did NOT fully collapse (ended 0.2521 vs the Oct run's 0.0). The trajectory differs from October because flash-linear-attention is unpinned in SkyRL's pyproject.toml, so the GDN kernel version drifted between the two runs.
